semantic_fragments.content: ME equipment or ME system with essential performance intended to actively keep alive or resuscitate a patient shall maintain its essential performance for a sufficient time or for a sufficient number of procedures when loss or failure of supply mains or near depletion of internal electrical power source occurred. The time or number of procedures remaining shall allow alternative life-supporting methods to be employed. Instructions for use shall disclose the time or number of procedures available following such loss or failure. ME equipment without internal electrical power source intended to keep alive patients shall be equipped with an alarm system including at least a medium priority alarm condition indicating power failure. ME equipment with internal electrical power source intended to keep alive patients shall be equipped with automatic switchover to internal electrical power source and an alarm indicating internal electrical power source is nearing insufficient remaining power.

For ME EQUIPMENT or ME SYSTEM with an INTERNAL ELECTRICAL POWER SOURCE, if simultaneous connection of the ME EQUIPMENT to the PATIENT and the SUPPLY MAINS is possible, then APPLIED PARTS and parts that are likely to come into contact with the PATIENT shall have two MOPP from the SUPPLY MAINS. However, parts which the PATIENT intentionally handles as the intended OPERATOR (e.g. touch keys, ENCLOSURE) while the ME EQUIPMENT is not being used for its intended medical function may be insulated with two MOOP from SUPPLY MAINS.

The risks associated with usability in the home healthcare environment for operator profiles including a lay operator when performing the usability engineering process include at least the following considerations: changes of controls, unexpected movement, potential for misconnection. Changes of controls were evaluated in the Usability test report.
